open_points.subject: check_request_shape value-schema inspection
open_points.text: must name an input port whose value_schema declares type string or integer
open_points.question: How is the JSON Schema stored in the value_schema string to be parsed, and which schema forms count as declaring a type (for example type arrays, unions, references, or malformed JSON)?
options: Parse value_schema as JSON and accept only a literal top-level type string
Accept equivalent JSON Schema forms such as type arrays or unions
Treat malformed or unsupported schemas as a misfit
open_points.default_guess: Parse it as JSON, require the relevant top-level type string, and treat parsing or unsupported forms as a misfit.

open_points.subject: check_request_shape placeholder processing
open_points.text: the placeholders taken in name order by Unicode code point
open_points.question: Are repeated occurrences of the same placeholder checked once or once per occurrence, and how are equal names ordered?
options: Check unique placeholder names once
Check every occurrence, sorting by name and retaining path order for ties
open_points.default_guess: Check unique placeholder names once in code-point order.

open_points.subject: check_request_shape input lookup
open_points.text: must name an input port
open_points.question: What happens if input_ports contains two ports with the same name, and which declaration represents a placeholder or non-placeholder input?
options: Treat duplicate port declarations as a misfit
Use the first matching port
Use the last matching port
Check every matching port
open_points.default_guess: Treat duplicate input names as a misfit.

open_points.subject: check_request_shape GET/DELETE rule ordering
open_points.text: input ports in name order by Unicode code point must have no file carriage and every input that is not a placeholder must have a value_schema
open_points.question: For one port that violates both carriage and schema, is carriage checked before schema, and are all carriage checks completed before any schema checks?
options: For each sorted port, check carriage then schema
Check carriage for every sorted port, then schema for every sorted port
open_points.default_guess: For each port in name order, check carriage first and then its schema.

open_points.subject: check_request_shape output validation
open_points.text: an output port of file carriage must be the only output port and must have cardinality one
open_points.question: In what order are multiple output ports examined, and which port/rule is named when more than one output violation exists?
options: Inspect outputs in supplied tuple order
Inspect outputs by Unicode port-name order
Reject the first file port after separately checking output count
open_points.default_guess: Inspect file outputs in Unicode name order, checking exclusivity before cardinality.

open_points.subject: check_request_shape failure reasons
open_points.text: a reason naming the first failing rule
open_points.question: What exact reason strings identify each rule and port?
options: Use stable implementation-defined sentences
Use machine-like rule identifiers plus the port name
open_points.default_guess: Use deterministic sentences containing a short rule identifier and the port name.

open_points.subject: prepare_request instance class
open_points.text: an instance_class that is None or not a known class counting as the imported DEFAULT_INSTANCE_CLASS constant
open_points.question: Which instance-class values are known, since no complete known-class constant is imported?
options: Only DEFAULT_INSTANCE_CLASS and members of PLAIN_HTTP_INSTANCE_CLASSES are known
Every non-None string is known
There is an unstated registry
open_points.default_guess: Treat the default and plain-HTTP class constants as the complete known set.

open_points.subject: prepare_request base URL validation
open_points.text: an absolute http or https URL with a host
open_points.question: Are user information, fragments, existing queries, invalid ports, non-ASCII hosts, empty ports, or unusual but parseable authorities valid base URLs?
options: Accept anything the standard URL parser recognizes with scheme and hostname
Apply strict RFC URL and authority validation
Reject query, fragment, and user-information components
open_points.default_guess: Require an http/https scheme, parser-recognized hostname, and valid port, while otherwise preserving accepted components.

open_points.subject: prepare_request URL construction
open_points.text: base_url without one trailing slash followed by the declared path
open_points.question: Does “without one trailing slash” remove exactly one slash or all trailing slashes, and is a separator inserted when the declared path lacks a leading slash?
options: Remove exactly one trailing slash and concatenate path verbatim
Remove all trailing slashes and prepend one slash to path
Normalize the join as a URL path
open_points.default_guess: Remove exactly one final slash and concatenate the declared path verbatim.

open_points.subject: prepare_request existing URL query and fragment
open_points.text: Builds the URL as base_url ... followed by the declared path
open_points.question: How are generated query parameters combined when base_url or the declared path already contains a query or fragment?
options: Preserve and append to an existing query
Reject such base URLs or paths
Treat question marks and fragments as literal declared URL text
open_points.default_guess: Preserve an existing query, append generated parameters with &, and place them before any fragment.

open_points.subject: prepare_request required-header validation
open_points.text: not an HTTP field-name token ... or holds a control character
open_points.question: Which HTTP grammar/version defines a field-name token, and does “control character” include DEL, tabs, or non-ASCII control characters?
options: Use RFC 9110 token and reject C0 plus DEL
Reject only C0 characters
Reject all Unicode control categories
open_points.default_guess: Use the RFC token grammar and reject C0 characters and DEL, including tab.

open_points.subject: prepare_request header collisions
open_points.text: The headers sent are exactly: one host header ... the instance's other required headers ... the credential header ... content-type and content-length
open_points.question: What happens when the credential header or a required header collides case-insensitively with Host, Accept-Encoding, Content-Type, Content-Length, or another kernel-generated header?
options: Return required_header_repeated
Allow duplicate wire headers
Let generated headers replace supplied headers
Reject only collisions covered explicitly before credential resolution
open_points.default_guess: Return required_header_repeated for required-header collisions and input_not_placeable for a credential collision.

open_points.subject: prepare_request credential header validity
open_points.text: then the credential ... the credential header
open_points.question: Must the resolved credential header name and value pass the same syntax checks as required headers, and what result represents an invalid credential header?
options: Validate it and return credential_unresolved
Validate it and return required_header_invalid
Trust the resolver completely
open_points.default_guess: Trust the credential resolver completely.

open_points.subject: prepare_request unexpected credential failures
open_points.text: CredentialUnresolvedError giving credential_unresolved
open_points.question: What happens if resolve_service_credential raises another exception?
options: Propagate it
Convert every resolver exception to credential_unresolved
open_points.default_guess: Convert only CredentialUnresolvedError and propagate other programming failures.

open_points.subject: prepare_request input payload access

open_points.question: How can the function identify a payload's port, payload kind, JSON value, or file bytes without declared PortPayload fields and while reflective probing is forbidden?

Assume an undisclosed tagged-union API
Parse model serialization despite the reflective-access ban

open_points.subject: prepare_request input correspondence

open_points.question: What happens for missing inputs, duplicate payloads for one port, payloads naming undeclared ports, a payload with the wrong kind, or payload order differing from port order?
options: Return input_not_placeable at the first sorted affected port
Ignore undeclared and duplicate payloads
Use the first or last duplicate payload

open_points.subject: prepare_request JSON payload decoding
open_points.text: a placeholder value is not a non-null string or integer
open_points.question: How is canonical_json in JsonPayload decoded, and what happens for invalid UTF-8, invalid JSON, duplicate members, or non-canonical JSON bytes?
options: Parse any valid JSON bytes and use the resulting value
Require RFC 8785 canonical bytes exactly
Treat malformed input as input_not_placeable
open_points.default_guess: Parse JSON strictly with duplicate rejection and return input_not_placeable if parsing fails, without requiring the supplied bytes already be canonical.

open_points.subject: prepare_request numeric values
open_points.text: a string, integer, number or boolean is one parameter ... numbers and booleans written as their canonical JSON text
open_points.question: Which numeric domain is supported, particularly arbitrary precision, negative zero, NaN, and infinity?
options: Use the RFC 8785/JSON number domain
Use Python int and finite float behavior
Accept arbitrary Decimal values
open_points.default_guess: Accept integers and finite JSON numbers only and serialize them using RFC 8785 rules.

open_points.subject: prepare_request input schema enforcement
open_points.text: then input placement, which gives input_not_placeable
open_points.question: Does preparation also call fit_port_value or otherwise enforce each input port's schema, carriage, cardinality, and size, or does it validate only whether the runtime value can be placed?
options: Validate placement types only
Run fit_port_value before placement
Assume an upstream module already validated all payloads
open_points.default_guess: Validate only the placement requirements stated here and assume upstream contract validation.

open_points.subject: prepare_request file-input detection
open_points.text: with a file input the body is multipart/form-data
open_points.question: Is the multipart branch selected by a declared file-carriage port or only by a supplied file payload, and what happens if such a port is absent, malformed, or used as a path placeholder?
options: Select from port declarations
Select from supplied payload kinds
Return input_not_placeable for any inconsistent declaration/payload combination
open_points.default_guess: Select from declared non-path file ports and return input_not_placeable if their payloads are inconsistent.

open_points.subject: prepare_request file media type
open_points.text: Content-Type, the port's media type for a file part
open_points.question: What Content-Type is emitted when a file port's media_type is None, which the Port model permits?
options: Return input_not_placeable
Use application/octet-stream
Omit Content-Type despite the exactly-two-headers rule
open_points.default_guess: Return input_not_placeable.

open_points.subject: prepare_request multipart serialization
open_points.text: the body is multipart/form-data with one part per input
open_points.question: How is the boundary chosen, how are names and filenames quoted or escaped, and what exact CRLF, preamble, epilogue, and terminal-boundary bytes are used?
options: Generate a random standards-compliant boundary
Derive a deterministic boundary from part data
Use a fixed boundary after checking it does not occur in content
open_points.default_guess: Derive a deterministic collision-free boundary and use conventional CRLF MIME framing.

open_points.subject: prepare_request value cardinality in multipart
open_points.text: one part per input not used in the path ... one part per file in list order for a many file port
open_points.question: Does a many value port produce one JSON part containing the whole list or one part per list element?
options: One part containing the canonical JSON array
One part per list element
open_points.default_guess: Use one part containing the complete canonical JSON array.

open_points.subject: prepare_request wire-header order and spelling
open_points.text: The headers sent are exactly
open_points.question: In what order are wire_headers emitted, and what casing is used for generated Host, Accept-Encoding, Content-Type, and Content-Length names?
options: Use the prose order and conventional title case
Sort all headers case-insensitively
Preserve required-header positions and use lowercase generated names

open_points.subject: prepare_request default Host value
open_points.text: otherwise the authority of base_url exactly as written
open_points.question: Does the Host value include user information, an explicit default port, IPv6 brackets, or percent-encoding, and which substring is the authority when the URL is unusual?
options: Use the complete raw authority substring
Use host plus explicit port but exclude user information
Use the URL parser's normalized netloc

open_points.subject: prepare_request description header ordering

Sort by lower-cased name and value
Disallow all duplicate lower-cased names

open_points.subject: prepare_request description redaction
open_points.text: each with its value except the credential header and content-length, which appear with value None
open_points.question: How is the credential header distinguished later if its name collides with content-length or another header, and are all same-named occurrences redacted?
options: Redact the exact credential HeaderField occurrence
Redact every header with the credential name
Prevent all such collisions

open_points.subject: prepare_request request digest
open_points.text: request_digest is content_identity of the canonical JSON of the description
open_points.question: Which imported IdentitySubject representation is passed to content_identity, and what exact JSON object shape and enum representation constitute the description's canonical JSON?
options: Use JsonTextContent around the canonical JSON text
Use BytesContent containing canonical bytes
Use an undisclosed direct RequestDescription identity conversion
open_points.default_guess: Serialize only the listed RequestDescription fields with enum values and explicit nulls, canonicalize under RFC 8785, and pass it as JsonTextContent.

open_points.subject: prepare_request failure reasons
open_points.text: with a reason naming it

Use the DetailCode value plus an optional name

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request credential discovery

Add unstated knowledge of credential-header names
Treat every redacted non-content-length header as credential

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request credential byte encoding
open_points.text: contains the bytes of the credential value sent
open_points.question: Which encoding turns the header string into searched bytes, and what happens if the credential is empty or cannot be encoded under the HTTP wire encoding?

Search Latin-1 wire bytes
Treat an empty credential as matching every body
Skip searching an empty credential

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request DNS deadline
open_points.text: MUST bound connecting, writing and reading the whole response by one deadline
open_points.question: How is blocking operating-system name resolution bounded and cancelled using only standard-library facilities?

Resolve in a worker and time out waiting
Use a lower-level platform-specific resolver

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request write-state classification
open_points.text: before the first request byte was written
open_points.question: Does a successful partial socket send count as written even if the client API later reports failure, and how is that fact observed when a buffered HTTP implementation is used?
options: Track raw socket send progress byte by byte
Treat entering the library's send call as possibly written
Treat successful completion of the headers write as first-byte written
open_points.default_guess: Use low-level socket writes and mark written after the first positive send result.

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request end-of-stream handling

open_points.question: When is end of stream a transport failure rather than the normal terminator of a response body without Content-Length, and what happens to a truncated Content-Length or chunked body?

Every EOF before a framing-defined end is failure
Treat any EOF after request write as the listed failure
open_points.default_guess: Treat EOF as normal for valid close-delimited bodies and as failure when declared framing is incomplete.

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request interim responses

open_points.question: Which interim responses are skipped, when does the client conclude that the response contained only 1xx, and is 101 treated as final or interim?

Treat 101 as final and unsupported
Treat the first 1xx as the result
open_points.default_guess: Skip 100–199 responses, including 101, and classify as only-1xx if the stream ends before a final response.

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request response ceiling

Use framing metadata when available and otherwise cannot distinguish equality from overflow
Interpret “read at most” as retain at most, while allowing a probe

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request response header ceiling
open_points.text: a status line and header section longer together than the imported ... constant
open_points.question: Which raw bytes count toward this limit—line terminators, the empty terminating line, interim response sections, and folded or rejected syntax—and is the limit per response or cumulative?

Count only status/header text excluding line terminators
Apply the limit separately to each interim and final response
open_points.default_guess: Count all raw bytes including line endings cumulatively across interim responses and the final header section.

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request unlisted status codes

options: Treat them as malformed status lines
Treat all non-listed statuses as operation_failed
Classify by integer hundreds digit without restriction
open_points.default_guess: Reject them as malformed status lines.

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request transfer decoding

Decode both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Encoding
Treat unsupported transfer codings as malformed transport
open_points.default_guess: Decode valid HTTP transfer framing such as chunked, do not decode Content-Encoding, and treat unsupported transfer codings as malformed.

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request direct invalid PreparedRequest shapes

Return contract_violation
Use the first file port

Split both values at the first semicolon and compare trimmed text
Compare only a normalized type/subtype from the response

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request JSON parsing
open_points.text: UTF-8 text parsing as one JSON object without duplicate member names

Use Python's default json semantics
Reject any number not exactly representable as an IEEE-754 double

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request output candidate construction

Use a different candidate shape for many cardinality
Pass the complete response object candidate

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request output ordering

open_points.question: In what order are multiple JsonPayload outputs returned?
options: The declared output_ports tuple order
Unicode port-name order
JSON member order

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request canonical output bytes

Preserve the member's original source bytes

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request credential search versus truncation

Include the overflow probe
Continue consuming and searching the entire body

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request failure detail on oversized bodies

Read only enough bytes for failure detail
Use all temporarily received bytes including an overflow probe

open_points.subject: send_prepared_request failure detail availability

open_points.question: Do malformed status/header responses, header-ceiling failures, and transport failures after partial body receipt count as an “answer,” and which accumulated bytes become their failure_detail?

Any received response bytes form an answer
Only responses with a parsed status are answers
